concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.note: Central topic of the torah. Discusses the value of thinking before speaking Torah insights. No bechina relationships stated; the torah is advisory/eitza in nature.
Mentioned as a prerequisite for Torah speech. Linked via eitza (cause-and-effect), not bechina (shared nature).
The act of speaking Torah. Paired with machshava (thought) but through a sequential process, not shared-nature equivalence.

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.concept_en: Four stages of God's Torah review
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.note: The Midrash (B'R 40) describes four stages: seeing, counting, preparing, investigating (raa, visapra, hechina, chakara). These are sequential stages, not bechina-type shared-nature groupings. They describe God's process of reviewing Torah four times before revealing it.
The spread of holy works from tzaddikim of recent generations makes Torah innovation easier. Mentioned as a historical observation, not a bechina relationship.
